newsitem.title: USA: CTAs do well in forex, bonds, natgas in November.
newsitem.headline: CTAs do well in forex, bonds, natgas in November.

text.p: Commodity trading advisors (CTAs) whose strategies are based on technical analysis, rather than on an analysis of economic fundamentals, registered the best returns in world commodity markets in November, according to in fund monitor TASS Management Ltd.
The best gains came in the currency, bond and natural gas markets, TASS Management chief executive Nicola Meaden said.
Nine of the top-performing commodity trading programs were trend followers, with the top ones posting returns in excess of 20 percent for the month.

"Trades in the currency and bond markets seemed to benefit many of the top programs," she said. "Strategies tied to going long British pounds and shorting the Swiss franc were profitable as was going long in the US and foreign bond markets."
British pounds saw a four year high against the US dollar at $1.6905 in November, while the US 30 year long bond rallied to nine month highs.
"In addition, going long natural gas also seemed to a profitable strategy," Meaden said.
NYMEX nearby natgas futures saw an all time record high at $4.050 per mmbtu in late November.
Year-to-date through November, the average CTA program monitored by TASS was up 19.42 pct.
September, October and November were the strongest months this year, with the average fund appreciating 15.92 pct in that period.
The monthly "TASS Flash Report" follows the performance of 68 CTA programs, each with a minimum of $45 million under management.
TASS Management Inc is a London-based research company which tracks the performance of about 1,600 "alternative investment" managers and funds globally with $9 billion under management.
"Alternative investments" include hedge funds, CTA programs, managed currency managers, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
